Thanks again for the conversation earlier — excited to get this expansion queued as part of your upcoming renewal. Per our discussion, Redwood can add an additional reserved GPU pool (8x A100 equivalent nodes) and commit a throughput SLA tier for the next 12 months.

Attached: capacity_specs_v4.pdf (deltas vs current pool) and an initial traffic_sculpting_plan.xlsx with a suggested 4-stage migration ramp. High level:

Folks — I sketched a concise MOP and included the critical technical hedges. Draft below (I’ll push the full .md to the shared drive and attach the short MOP to the final email).

MOP (summary for Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC window)
1) Provisioning & validation (T0):
   - Confirm API returns new pool "acme-reserved-v2" with expected node count (8 nodes).
   - Verify GPU drivers/kernels on nodes and that perf bench passes (smoke lat/throughput).
2) KV cache pre-warm (T0 + 30m):
   - Run automated warm-job (script: scripts/warm_kv.sh) to pre-populate top 200 keys per model.
   - If warm-job fails, skip canary and fall back to legacy routing.
3) Canary rollout (T0 + 60m):
   - Redirect 1% of traffic for 30m — measure P50/P95/P99 and token-generation error rates.
   - After 30m, if P99 <= baseline + 20ms and error delta < 0.1%, move to 5% for 2 hours.
4) Ramp windows (T0 + day):
   - 5% -> 25% over 6 hours -> 50% over next 12 hours -> steady-state (as agreed).
   - Use shard-aware routing to minimize cross-pool cache miss spikes.
5) Traffic sculpting rules
   - Keep short-context queries (<128 tokens) on legacy pool until 25% ramp to avoid small-request scheduling churn on new pool.
   - Heavy-batch/long-context sessions preferentially routed to new reserved pool once warm.
6) Rollback criteria
   - Any sustained P99 regression > baseline + 50ms for 20 minutes OR error rate spike >0.5% triggers immediate 50% rollback and ops call.
7) Post-cutover validation
   - 24-hour quality sweep: sample 1% of requests across critical routes and run automated prompt-level checks (we should capture checks in the shared sheet).

SLA/Metric notes:
- We can commit to a P99 latency target for committed throughput up to X qps (see capacity_specs_v4.pdf for numerics). We will include the specific P99 in the addendum with the committed qps bucket.

Ops asks for customer:
- Provide a list of 3 high-priority prompt templates to run quality checks during canary.
- Confirm procurement signoff timeline.

I’ll prepare the one-page MOP (mop-reserved-pool-migration.md) and attach scripts. If this looks good I’ll move to a runbook format by EOD Tue.

—Rishi
